The Alternation Between the Smooth Block and the Rest

Source: R/statmod.R
statmod_alternate.Rd

Fits the terms whose penalties are twice differentiable in one system and each remaining block by a method of its own, alternating until the objective stops moving.

Usage

statmod_alternate(
  spec,
  design,
  blocks,
  hyper,
  inner_optimizer,
  beta,
  expected,
  emethod,
  maxit,
  tol,
  vb,
  working_budget = 500L,
  hold_refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

spec

The specification.

design

The design.

blocks

The split of the terms into smooth and sparse, as statmod_blocks() returns it.

hyper

The hyperparameters, held fixed for the whole call.

inner_optimizer

How the smooth block is fitted: iwls() or an optimizers7 optimizer.

beta

The starting coefficients, stacked into one numeric vector.

expected

TRUE for the expected information, FALSE for the observed one.

emethod

The method that obtains the expected information: NULL (the closed form of the family where it has one, and distributions7::expect_opg() otherwise) or an object that inherits from distributions7::ExpectMethod. It is read only where the expected information is used.

maxit, tol

The budget in passes and the relative tolerance on the objective, as method_budget() read them off inner_optimizer.

vb

The resolved verbosity, as verbosity() returns it.

working_budget

How many working fits fit_working() may take. The bootstrap excursions of statmod_boot_restart() pass a short one: an excursion needs to travel, not to converge.

hold_refresh

TRUE holds every frozen break-point block at its committed positions: the fit is then an ordinary smooth fit, and the schedule is neither read off nor advanced. The outer machinery passes it at every criterion evaluation, path point and fold. A working phase inside each evaluation would multiply the cost of the fit, and a break-point that moves between evaluations makes the criterion depend on the path of the search. The positions are refined once, by the full alternation that statmod() runs at the chosen hyperparameters before the restarts.

Value

A list of nine:

par

the stacked coefficients reached.

value

the penalized objective there, not averaged.

converged

a single logical. Where a term recomputes its own block, the verdict is the objective's together with that term's own flags, and the flag of the smooth block is not part of it. Beside a kinked block or a structural term it also requires alternation_settled() at the point. Where the fit does not alternate between blocks, it is the flag of the inner method.

obj

the objective object that the last pass used.

note

the note element of the last smooth fit, as fit_smooth() returns it.

aliased

the sorted stacked positions that the pivot left out.

hist_blocks

a list of one-row data frames, one for each block fitted in each pass, with pass, block, objective, change, iterations and converged.

hist_inner

a list of data frames, one for each pass in which the smooth fit recorded steps, holding the inner history with the columns pass and block added.

spec

the specification after the last pass, with the SCAD and MCP curvatures that the fit used.

Details

The outer search calls this function once for each hyperparameter value that it tries, warm-started from the previous coefficients, so a whole fit at one point of the search is one call.

One pass fits the smooth block (beside a structural term of the filter shape, the joint system of the coefficients and the term's parameters), then the structural block of a term of the likelihood shape, then each kinked block while the other blocks are held, and then commits the schedule of any refreshable term. The passes stop when the relative change of the objective falls below tol. The verdict is the inner fit's flag where the fit does not alternate between blocks. Otherwise it also requires alternation_settled() (the Newton decrement of the smooth part and the KKT decrement of each coefficient that a kinked penalty holds at zero, both within mode_error_limit()), and statmod_refresh_settled() where the model has refreshable terms.

See also

statmod() for the fit that this performs, fit_smooth() and sparse_fit() for the two halves of a pass, and statmod_boot_restart(), which calls this repeatedly.
